You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 356b57752c91cffb35356abe6647065bf0edcad1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Rafael J. Wysocki" <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Feb 2018 12:10:59 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] platform/x86: intel-hid: Reset wakeup capable flag on removal

The intel-hid device will not be able to wake up the system any more
after removing the notify handler provided by its driver, so make
its sysfs attributes reflect that.

Fixes: ef884112e55c (platform: x86: intel-hid: Wake up the system from suspend-to-idle)
Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c b/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c
index d1a01311c1a2..5e3df194723e 100644
--- a/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c
+++ b/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c
@@ -376,6 +376,7 @@ static int intel_hid_remove(struct platform_device *device)
 {
 	acpi_handle handle = ACPI_HANDLE(&device->dev);
 
+	device_init_wakeup(&device->dev, false);
 	acpi_remove_notify_handler(handle, ACPI_DEVICE_NOTIFY, notify_handler);
 	intel_hid_set_enable(&device->dev, false);
 	intel_button_array_enable(&device->dev, false);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c`**
- Added a line to reset the wakeup capable flag by calling `device_init_wakeup(&device->dev, false);` within the `intel_hid_remove` function. This change ensures that the device will not be able to wake up the system after its removal.

### Relationships
The modification in the `intel-hid.c` file directly addresses the issue of the intel-hid device retaining its ability to wake the system after it has been removed. By resetting the wakeup capable flag, the patch ensures that the sysfs attributes accurately reflect the device's state, thereby preventing any unintended wake-up behavior after the device is no longer present. This change is a fix for a previously introduced functionality that allowed the device to wake the system from suspend-to-idle, as noted in the fix reference.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The bug arises from the fact that the intel-hid device retains its ability to wake the system even after it has been removed, due to the lack of a mechanism to reset the wakeup capable flag in the device's sysfs attributes. This can lead to unexpected behavior where the system may wake up from suspend when it should not, as the device is no longer present to handle such actions.
        
        Commit message:
        platform/x86: intel-hid: Reset wakeup capable flag on removal

The intel-hid device will not be able to wake up the system any more
after removing the notify handler provided by its driver, so make
its sysfs attributes reflect that.

Fixes: ef884112e55c (platform: x86: intel-hid: Wake up the system from suspend-to-idle)
Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>

 	/*
 	 * Even if we failed to shut off the event stream, we can still

 	 */

 }
